title: General functional encryption from plain LWE
formal: Does the specified ordinary decisional LWE assumption imply public-key functional encryption for all polynomial-size Boolean circuits, with adaptive indistinguishability security against arbitrarily polynomially many colluding functional-key queries?
definitions:
The security parameter is lambda, supplied in unary. Efficient algorithms are uniform probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machines; security is against nonuniform probabilistic polynomial-size circuit families with polynomially many oracle queries. A function is negligible if it is eventually smaller than lambda^{-c} for every constant c>0. All message, instance and witness lengths in a security experiment are polynomial in lambda. No random oracle, trusted hardware or additional computational assumption is available.

The selected plain-LWE assumption is decisional LWE in dimension lambda, with q the least prime at least lambda^3 and integer error distribution assigning probability proportional to exp(-pi e^2/lambda^2) to each e in Z, reduced modulo q. For every polynomial m(lambda), a uniform matrix A in Z_q^{m by lambda}, a uniform secret s in Z_q^lambda and independent errors e give (A,As+e) computationally indistinguishable from (A,u) with uniform independent u in Z_q^m. Hardness is against the circuit adversaries above with negligible distinguishing advantage. This explicitly fixes polynomial modulus and inverse-polynomial relative noise; it does not assume evasive LWE, subexponential security or leakage resilience. It is an editorial parameter choice, not a claim that every formulation called LWE is equivalent.

Setup(1^lambda,1^n,1^s) generates a public encryption key pk and master secret msk for n-bit messages and circuits of at most s gates, with n,s polynomially bounded in lambda but otherwise arbitrary. KeyGen(msk,C) produces a functional secret key for any such Boolean circuit C with n input bits and a polynomial-length output. Enc(pk,m) encrypts m; Dec(sk_C,c) outputs C(m) for an honest ciphertext except with negligible error. All algorithms have polynomial cost in their explicit parameters and inputs. The circuit-size bound is allowed at setup; no collusion-count bound is supplied.

In the adaptive security game an adversary receives pk and requests keys for circuits of its choice. It then submits equal-length messages m0,m1 such that C(m0)=C(m1) for every circuit queried so far. It receives Enc(pk,m_b) for uniform b and may continue requesting keys subject to the same equality condition. Its advantage in guessing b must be negligible. The adversary can make any polynomial number of requests, with no fixed exponent built into the scheme; setup and ciphertext sizes do not grow with a declared number of users or queries. Only admissible adversaries satisfying all equality restrictions are considered. Public encryption already lets them generate other ciphertexts. No decryption oracle or function-hiding guarantee is required. This selects adaptive indistinguishability, not simulation-based security.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction, correctness proof and adaptive-security reduction using only the stated LWE assumption, or refute this precise implication. Security for a bounded declared number of keys, for only inner products, or under stronger combined assumptions does not meet the target.
context:
Functional encryption separates the ability to encrypt publicly from the ability to learn particular functions through restricted keys; its different security definitions must be distinguished.

Dynamic bounded-collusion constructions move the collusion bound to encryption time but still let ciphertext size depend on that bound. They do not provide the unrestricted collusion guarantee here.
why: This asks whether a central lattice assumption supports general fine-grained access to encrypted data.

import_provenance.original_title: General functional encryption from plain LWE
import_provenance.original_statement: Construct public-key functional encryption for arbitrary polynomial-size circuits, secure against any polynomial number of colluding functional-key holders, from ordinary LWE alone. This is an assumption-focused continuation of Boneh, Sahai and Waters’ general functional-encryption program; bounded-collusion constructions do not meet the target.

sentences: Public encryption protects messages while functional keys reveal circuit outputs.
Challenge messages must agree under every requested circuit.
Keys may be requested adaptively before and after the challenge.
The number of colluding keys has no declared bound built into the scheme.
The target uses ordinary LWE and adaptive indistinguishability rather than stronger assumptions or simulation.
